newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate steady despite higher turnover.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate steady despite higher turnover.

text.p: * Big banks borrow heavily to cover weekend deficiencies
The Philippine call loan rate held its ground at 10.53125 percent on Monday despite heightened demand for overnight money, traders said.
"There were a lot of borrowers in the market. But the system is still liquid, so the rate remained at 10.53125 percent," one trader said.
He said big borrowers swamped the market in order to cover their reserve deficiencies over the weekend.
"After today, we will see the demand easing to less than 10 billion pesos," he added. A total of 17.192 billion pesos changed hands with done rates ranging from 10.53125 to 10.8125 percent.
The remittance of witholding tax, which was estimated to be around 5.0 billion pesos, further aggravated the deficieny positions of the banks.

The secondary Treasury bill market was quiet ahead of the the weekly T-bill auction, although there were banks raising their offered rates to sell off their low-yielding T-bill holdings in anticipation of higher T-bill rates.
Traders said they were expecting a slight uptick in the rates, especially in the three-month and six-month rates, after the Central Bank raised its special T-bill rates late last week.
They expected the auction rates to rise by 5.0 to 10.0 basis points during the auction.
Three-month bills were being offered between 10.40 to 10.680 percent, while six-month bills were being offered between 11.10 to 11.225 percent.
One-year bills were being sold between 11.45 to 11.60 percent.
